/** Lowercase ASCII letters and digits of `text`, with each other run collapsed to one '-', trimmed of '-'. */
export function slugify(text) {
  return text
    .replace(/[A-Z]/g, (c) => c.toLowerCase())
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
}

# Constraints (C-nn ledger)

C-1 — Every module under src/ is a pure ES module with no runtime dependencies and no I/O.
C-2 — Every exported function is covered by node --test tests under test/, one test file per module.
# Invariants

- `npm test` passes on the integration branch.
- `package.json` declares no dependencies.

reasons: The spec's B1–B3 match the pageId section of contract one, word for word: slugify(title)-n, the 'page' fallback with the '!!!'/3 example, and a RangeError for a non-integer or non-positive n.
F1 holds at this tip: src/slug.js exports slugify, which arrived through the unit slug candidate commit already on the integration branch. The import that B1 requires will therefore resolve.

B4 and the page-id lane together satisfy C-2 (one test file per module). C-1 purity follows from the contract and the architecture rules. No witness gap would let a plausible wrong build pass: B2 rules out an empty slug giving '-3', and B3 covers both non-positive and non-integer n.

premises.claim: slugify is exported by src/slug.js at the unit tip, and its output never starts or ends with '-', so an empty slug is the only case that needs the 'page' fallback.
C-2 requires one node --test file per module, and B4 provides it as test/page-id.test.js.
The contract defines pageId's fallback and its RangeError behaviour exactly as B2 and B3 state them.
